releases.name: @wakeshift/cli 0.1.0
releases.body:
The first release.

- **`init`** makes an app key on your computer, writes it to `.env` (git-ignored, readable only by you), and creates the app through a console link you confirm, waiting until it exists.
- **`keys new`** adds a new key to an existing app the same way.
- **`status`** shows the app, its key and the events Wakeshift has from your server.
- **`verify`** acts as an agent against your running server: it calls the tool that subscribes, checks its description and reply, emits a test event (or runs your trigger) only when nobody else is subscribed with those arguments, waits for the wake, cleans up, and says what to fix.
- The key is never printed, never taken as an argument, and redacted from everything relayed.

releases.name: Installers v1.4.31
releases.body:
Wakeshift's installers, version 2026.11.05.0621+029c19c. Built from wakeshift/wakeshift@029c19cdec06, which isn't published here as its own export; the tag marks main when the release was made.

Install for your agent (for example Codex): `curl -fsSL https://github.com/wakeshift/connectors/releases/latest/download/codex.sh | sh`.
Each script carries the SHA-256 of what it downloads from this release and refuses anything else.

The `wakeshift-connect-*.tgz`, `wakeshift-opencode-*.tgz` and `wakeshift-openclaw-*.tgz` files are this release's npm packages (`@wakeshift/connect`, its platform packages, `@wakeshift/opencode` and `@wakeshift/openclaw`), published to npm from here with provenance.

To check a release by hand, with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/system_config/installation/):

```sh
cosign verify-blob --bundle SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-identity 'https://github.com/wakeshift/wakeshift/.github/workflows/installers.yml@refs/tags/v1.4.31' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com SHA256SUMS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
```
